public_rationale: The decisive missing fact is the cost of capacity attributable to the original OpenAI agreement. Customer payments, company-wide spending and one financing facility are different measures. Management later said financing for that agreement was complete, but that does not establish its full cost or refute a March warning about possible financing difficulty. The quantified spending-and-funding assertion remains unresolved.
limitations: Later successful financing cannot disprove an earlier statement that access might be difficult.
The hedge about possible access is not independently scored as a failed prediction.
No accounting-basis or project-scope substitution is used to turn company-wide figures into OpenAI-specific costs.

our_interpretation: Assess the spending obligation and funding position asserted to exist at publication, not a forecast that financing would certainly fail.
Tens of billions means at least approximately $20 billion of required spending attributable to serving the original OpenAI agreement.
The post's surrounding press-based financial projections indicate an estimate, not a stated GAAP measure.
Use the latest pre-post reported balance-sheet date, December 31, 2024, together with financing and contract changes disclosed through March 24, 2025.
Does not have concerns existing resources. Future financing may be needed without being impossible.
The possible-access clause is a risk qualification. It is not an independently falsifiable prediction that borrowing will fail.
criteria.support_condition: A credible budget isolates at least approximately $20 billion of necessary spending for the original OpenAI contract and shows that contemporaneously available resources fall short.
criteria.contradiction_condition: A reliable complete budget places required OpenAI-specific spending materially below that threshold, or dated funding records show the required amount was already available.
